units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
You need not wait, Mabel. Remember, Lady Basildon is expecting you.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Oh! I must shake hands with Lady Markby. She is delightful. I love being scolded by her.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Enter MASON.
Lady Markby. Mrs. Cheveley.
units.name: MASON

units.text: Enter LADY MARKBY and MRS. CHEVELEY.
Advancing to meet them .
Dear Lady Markby, how nice of you to come and see me!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Shakes hands with her , and bows somewhat distantly to MRS. CHEVELEY.
Won’t you sit down, Mrs. Cheveley?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Thanks. Isn’t that Miss Chiltern? I should like so much to know her.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Mabel, Mrs. Cheveley wishes to know you.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: MABEL CHILTERN gives a little nod .
CHEVELEY
units.name: MRS

units.text: Sitting down .
I thought your frock so charming last night, Miss Chiltern. So simple and . . . suitable.
units.name: MRS

units.text: Really? I must tell my dressmaker. It will be such a surprise to her. Good-bye, Lady Markby!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Going already?
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: I am so sorry but I am obliged to. I am just off to rehearsal. I have got to stand on my head in some tableaux.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: On your head, child? Oh! I hope not. I believe it is most unhealthy.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Takes a seat on the sofa next LADY CHILTERN.
But it is for an excellent charity: in aid of the Undeserving, the only people I am really interested in. I am the secretary, and Tommy Trafford is treasurer.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: And what is Lord Goring?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Oh! Lord Goring is president.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: The post should suit him admirably, unless he has deteriorated since I knew him first.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Reflecting .
You are remarkably modern, Mabel. A little too modern, perhaps. Nothing is so dangerous as being too modern. One is apt to grow old-fashioned quite suddenly. I have known many instances of it.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: What a dreadful prospect!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Ah! my dear, you need not be nervous. You will always be as pretty as possible. That is the best fashion there is, and the only fashion that England succeeds in setting.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: With a curtsey .
Thank you so much, Lady Markby, for England . . . and myself.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Goes out .
Turning to LADY CHILTERN.
Dear Gertrude, we just called to know if Mrs. Cheveley’s diamond brooch has been found.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Here?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Yes. I missed it when I got back to Claridge’s, and I thought I might possibly have dropped it here.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: I have heard nothing about it. But I will send for the butler and ask.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Touches the bell .
Oh, pray don’t trouble, Lady Chiltern. I dare say I lost it at the Opera, before we came on here.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Ah yes, I suppose it must have been at the Opera. The fact is, we all scramble and jostle so much nowadays that I wonder we have anything at all left on us at the end of an evening. I know myself that, when I am coming back from the Drawing Room, I always feel as if I hadn’t a shred on me, except a small shred of decent reputation, just enough to prevent the lower classes making painful observations through the windows of the carriage. The fact is that our Society is terribly over-populated. Really, some one should arrange a proper scheme of assisted emigration. It would do a great deal of good.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: I quite agree with you, Lady Markby. It is nearly six years since I have been in London for the Season, and I must say Society has become dreadfully mixed. One sees the oddest people everywhere.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: That is quite true, dear. But one needn’t know them. I’m sure I don’t know half the people who come to my house. Indeed, from all I hear, I shouldn’t like to.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Enter MASON.
What sort of a brooch was it that you lost, Mrs. Cheveley?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: A diamond snake-brooch with a ruby, a rather large ruby.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: I thought you said there was a sapphire on the head, dear?
units.name: LADY MARKBY
